{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-mbm7","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-worker6-4n5v: Ack::from_bytes panics on 2-byte complete ACKs","description":"Severity: P0 (crash/panic, DoS)

`Ack::from_bytes` and `Ack::from_bytes_for` at `fragment.rs:340` access `data[2]` unconditionally after only checking `data.len() < 2`. Complete ACKs are 2 bytes (`[rule_id, 0x40 | (window<<7)]`), so any 2-byte complete ACK causes an index-out-of-bounds panic.

This is reachable via the sender path: `FragmentSender::handle_ack_bytes` calls `Ack::from_bytes(data)` at line 583 without checking whether data is a complete ACK before calling the parser. A correct complete ACK (2 bytes) from a completed receiver would crash the sender.

The old code (before the rewrite) checked the complete bit BEFORE accessing `data[2]`. The new code reads `data[2]` unconditionally, then discards the complete bit (`let _complete = ...`).

**Fix:** Check for 2-byte complete ACKs before reading `data[2]`. Alternatively, check `data.len()` against the expected minimum (3 for non-complete) and handle complete ACKs specially.
